objective: Correct the existing CoS read-only broker patch; do not redesign unrelated code. The current policy is NOT acceptable because readonlySeatbeltProfile grants global file-read*, and runReadonlyCodex leaves CODEX_HOME unset while HOME points at the real home. Fix the OS boundary so the child can read only what it needs: the canonical project workspace, its private broker runtime/CODEX_HOME, the shipped Codex executable/application/system runtime files required to execute and establish TLS, and the existing ~/.codex/auth.json as a read-only credential reference. It must not gain general read access to unrelated user home files, and it must not write/rename/unlink the real auth file or real ~/.codex. Create a private 0700 CODEX_HOME inside the broker runtime and reference auth without copying or logging credential bytes. Keep writes limited to that runtime. Preserve network needed for Codex, and keep the single whole-process macOS seatbelt with no nested seatbelt. Strengthen tests so they fail if the policy contains an unconditional allow file-read*, if HOME/CODEX_HOME can direct state to real ~/.codex, or if source workspace write is permitted. Also ensure timeout cleanup owns the child process tree if needed. Keep the endpoint fixed-purpose and all current validation. Run focused tests/typecheck/diff check. Return success only if these requirements are actually met; otherwise name the exact blocker. Do not spawn agents.
constraints: Preserve unrelated changes and the useful parts of the prior patch.

previous_failure.error: Supervisor review rejected the first patch because its seatbelt used unconditional (allow file-read*) and it did not use a private per-run CODEX_HOME, violating Projects-only and read-only credential requirements.
